verdict.rationale: MotherDuck's own docs cover the whole loop without a dashboard. The remote MCP server lets an agent explore database schemas, tables and columns and execute read-only or read-write SQL. The DuckDB CLI and SDKs connect directly, with credentials saved locally for Python/CLI sessions. Governance comes from a read-only restriction, role-scoped Shares with include patterns, and an org-wide QUERY_HISTORY view. missing for 10: explicit documentation of headless/service-token authentication for agents and of the result-return format, plus independent hands-on corroboration of an agent running the full flow.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, my agent can run governed SQL end to end — authenticate, discover schemas, query, and read results back through a CLI or API with no dashboard in the loop

citations.quote:
With the remote MCP server, your agent can:
- Execute read-only and read-write SQL against your databases
- Explore database schemas, tables, and columns
If you are using Python or CLI and don't want to authenticate every session, you can securely save your credentials locally.
Install the DuckDB CLI and connect directly to MotherDuck
To restrict your AI assistant to read-only access, see Restricting to read-only access
The MD_INFORMATION_SCHEMA.QUERY_HISTORY view records every query run across your organization.
